analysis:
## Technical analysis

### The defining event — 200-DMA close breach; first since April 2025

NVDA closed at $190.27 on 2026-07-29, down −$6.74 / −3.42% from the July 28 reference close of $197.01. The close is below the 200-day moving average (~$192.72) — the first confirmed close below the 200-DMA since the April 2025 recovery. This is the most bearish technical event in the current framework period.

### Gate 3 progression — Conditions deteriorating simultaneously

| Condition | Threshold | Jul 27 | Jul 28 | Jul 29 | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVDA | > $200 | $199.27 ✗ | $197.01 ✗ | $190.27 ✗ | FAILED Day 3; below 200-DMA |
| SPX | > 7,460 | 7,411.98 ✗ | 7,438.41 ✗ | 7,316.15 ✗ | FAILED Day 5; gap widening |
| VIX | < 17 | 18.58 ✗ | 18.38 ✗ | ~20.5 ✗ | FAILED Day 4; elevated post-FOMC |

All three conditions are deteriorating simultaneously. The FOMC outcome has pushed VIX from 18.38 to ~20.5 in a single session — the opposite of what the July 28 analysis identified as the restoration scenario. SPX has fallen 122 points (from 7,438 to 7,316) since July 28 — the largest single-day SPX decline in the step-aside period.

### Trend — Six consecutive lower closes; 200-DMA broken

| Date | Close | Change | vs 200-DMA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jul 22 | $211.49 | supply zone top | above |
| Jul 23 | $208.76 | −$2.73 / −1.29% | above |
| Jul 24 | $206.44 | −$2.32 / −1.11% | above |
| Jul 27 | $199.27 | −$7.17 / −3.46% | above |
| Jul 28 | $197.01 | −$2.26 / −1.13% | above (intraday near-test) |
| Jul 29 | $190.27 | −$6.74 / −3.42% | BELOW (close breach) |

Total six-session decline: −$21.22 / −10.03% from $211.49. The pattern is now: acceleration (July 22-24: avg −$2.5/session), deceleration (July 27-28: avg −$4.7 but smaller on day 28), re-acceleration (July 29: −$6.74 triggered by FOMC). The re-acceleration on FOMC day removes the 'selling exhaustion' thesis from July 28.

### Volume — FOMC-day activity above average; confirmed breakdown

Specific July 29 NVDA volume data is unavailable, but context indicates above-average volume on the FOMC decision day. The broad market declined (DJIA −2.19%, SPX −1.52%), and a 200-DMA breakdown on elevated volume is technically more significant than a low-volume breach. The sell-the-200-DMA event is a defined systematic trigger — institutional and quant participants who use the 200-DMA as a line in the sand have now exited or shorted. This is not random selling; it is systematic deleveraging.

### The FOMC dynamic — Hawkish hold reverses the restoration thesis

The July 28 analysis identified three FOMC scenarios. The outcome was effectively Scenario 2.5 — between 'Hawkish Hold' (~20% odds) and 'Hike' (35% odds):
- **9-3 vote**: The three dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) were not anticipated at this intensity. This signals that the 'hold' was a close call and September is genuinely open.
- **10-year yield +7bps to 4.67%**: Yield spike confirms market read is hawkish. Higher yields = higher discount rate on NVDA's future cash flows = lower equity value.
- **Short Warsh statement**: The brevity of the statement was itself hawkish — no reassurance language, no forward guidance about rate path.
- **Result**: The one catalyst that could have restored all three Gate 3 conditions in a single session instead widened all three simultaneously.

### Strongest support — $185–$189 (Q1 2026 swing high / measured move)

With the 200-DMA breached on close, the next structural support is the $185-$189 zone:
- Prior Q1 2026 swing high that became support in March 2026
- Measured-move target from the $200 breakdown (prior resistance → new support pattern)
- Gap fill region from the June 2026 breakout
- The level where systematic 200-DMA breakdown shorts target for profit-taking
- Not the base case but now the primary downside destination if selling pressure continues

### Strongest resistance — $200.00 / $192.72 200-DMA

Two resistance layers above the close:
1. **200-DMA at $192.72** (2.3% above close): First overhead resistance; recovery above the 200-DMA would require buyers to absorb systematic sell pressure from 200-DMA breakdown strategies; a close above the 200-DMA before August 26 would be the first constructive technical signal since the step-aside began
2. **$200.00** (5.1% above close): The Gate 3 threshold; two weeks of closing rejections have established $200 as the primary resistance ceiling; Gate 3 restoration requires $200 + SPX 7,460 + VIX 17 simultaneously

### What invalidates the bear read

A FOMC-resolution event (Fed governor speech walking back hawkish dissents, August inflation data well below expectations, or geopolitical de-escalation) that compresses 10Y yields, pushes SPX above 7,460, and brings VIX below 17 — simultaneously with NVDA recovering above both the 200-DMA ($192.72) and the $200 Gate 3 threshold. This requires a 5.1% single-session move with macro confirmation. The earliest realistic catalyst is Microsoft/Meta earnings this week (if they add capex and trigger a tech sector recovery), though the Alphabet precedent suggests this is unlikely to be sufficient alone. August 26 NVDA earnings remains the highest-probability catalyst for all three conditions restoring simultaneously.
